transcript.text:
Let's narrow it down. Here are the most common causes, starting with the easiest to check:

## Quick checks (any oven)
1. Power: Is the clock/display on?
• Display is dead: Check your circuit breaker. Electric ovens usually use a double breaker, and it can trip halfway, so flip it fully OFF, then ON. Also make sure the oven is plugged in securely.
• Display works but oven won't heat: Keep reading.
2. Clock or timer settings: Many ovens won't heat if the clock isn't set (common after a power outage) or if a delay start or timed bake is active. Try setting the clock and cancelling any timers.
3. Control lock: Look for a lock icon. Usually you hold the "Lock" or "Cancel" button for 3–5 seconds to turn it off.
4. Self-clean lock: If you recently ran a self-clean cycle, the door may still be locked. Let it cool fully, or turn the breaker off for a minute to reset it.
5. Error codes: If there's a code (like F1, F3, or E1), tell me what it says along with your brand.

## Electric oven
• Bake element: Look at the coil at the bottom. If it's broken, blistered, or doesn't glow red after a few minutes, it likely needs replacing. This is a common and fairly cheap fix.
• If the broil works but bake doesn't (or vice versa), that points to a bad element.

## Gas oven
• Gas supply: Do the stovetop burners light? If not, check that the gas valve is on and your service is working.
• Igniter: Watch through the window. A healthy igniter glows bright orange and the gas lights within about 90 seconds. If it glows weakly with no flame, the igniter is probably worn out. This is the #1 cause of gas ovens not heating.
• If you smell gas, stop. Turn the oven off, don't use switches or flames, leave the house, and call your gas company.

---

To help further, could you tell me:
• Is it gas or electric?
• Does the display/clock light up?
• Does it do anything at all (click, fan, glow, error code)?
• Brand/model, if handy?
its electric, a Neff. display is flashing 0.00 and a little symbol. knobs do nothing. there was a power cut last night

This is almost certainly the power cut. Most Neff ovens won't heat until the clock is set again, and a flashing 0.00 means it's waiting for you to do that.

## Set the clock
The buttons vary by model, but try these in order:

1. Press the clock button (a clock or ⏲ symbol). On many Neff models the time starts flashing and you can set it with the + / – buttons or the control knob. Press the clock button again (or wait a few seconds) to confirm.
2. No clock button? Try pressing + and – together and then adjusting the time.
3. Touch control with a menu? Tap the display or press the clock/settings button and follow the prompts.

Once the time is set and stops flashing, try the oven knobs again.

## What's the little symbol?
That can change what you need to do:
• Letter "A" or "AUTO" flashing: The oven thinks it's in timed/automatic mode. Press the hand or saucepan symbol button (manual mode), or press two of the timer buttons together until the "A" clears.
• Key 🔑 or padlock: Child lock is on. Hold the key button for about 4–6 seconds until it disappears.
• Bell 🔔: That's the minute timer. It's usually harmless.
• Clock symbol: That's just prompting you to set the time, as above.

## If it still won't work
• Turn the breaker for the oven fully off for 1–2 minutes, then back on, and set the clock again.
• Let me know what the symbol looks like or your model number. It's usually on a sticker visible when you open the oven door, often starting with B, C, or U. Then I can give you exact button steps.
ok pressed the clock button and set the time and it came on and is heating now. thanks
Glad it's working! This will likely happen after any future power cut too, so if the oven ever goes dead with a flashing 0.00 again, just set the clock first.
